questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Destructuring Declarations”?
options: It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Apply destructuring declarations by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.
questions.answer_key: Apply destructuring declarations by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Destructuring Declarations”?
options: Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Destructuring Declarations”?
options: Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Destructuring Declarations removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
questions.answer_key: Destructuring Declarations removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Destructuring Declarations removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
